name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q01 - Geometry and bond angle of ammonia molecule

questiontext.text: Observe the structural diagram of the ammonia (\(\mathrm{NH_3}\)) molecule shown below and identify its molecular geometry and \(\mathrm{H-N-H}\) bond angle.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The diagram shows a central nitrogen atom (\(\mathrm{N}\)) bonded to three hydrogen atoms (\(\mathrm{H}\)) with \(\mathrm{N-H}\) bond lengths of \(101.7\ \mathrm{pm}\), one lone pair of electrons in an orbital lobe at the apex, and a \(\mathrm{H-N-H}\) bond angle of \(107.8^\circ\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
According to VSEPR theory, electron pairs around the central atom arrange themselves to minimise mutual electrostatic repulsion, with lone pair–bond pair repulsion being greater than bond pair–bond pair repulsion.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Nitrogen has 5 valence electrons and forms 3 single covalent bonds with hydrogen, leaving 1 lone pair. Thus, the steric number is \(3 + 1 = 4\), corresponding to \(sp^3\) hybridisation and a tetrahedral electron-pair geometry.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Because one of the four \(sp^3\) hybrid orbitals is occupied by a lone pair, the lone pair pushes the three \(\mathrm{N-H}\) bonding pairs slightly closer together, reducing the \(\mathrm{H-N-H}\) bond angle from the ideal tetrahedral angle of \(109.5^\circ\) to \(107.8^\circ\). Considering only the positions of the atomic nuclei, the three hydrogen atoms form a triangular base with nitrogen at the apex.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The bond angle \(107.8^\circ\) is consistent with one lone pair on an \(sp^3\)-hybridised central atom. Therefore, the ammonia molecule has a trigonal pyramidal geometry with a \(\mathrm{H-N-H}\) bond angle of \(107.8^\circ\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q02 - Reactivity and structure of white phosphorus

questiontext.text: The diagram below represents the molecular structure of white phosphorus (\(\mathrm{P_4}\)). Based on the structure, why is white phosphorus much more reactive than red phosphorus under normal conditions?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The diagram illustrates a discrete tetrahedral \(\mathrm{P_4}\) molecule of white phosphorus in which each phosphorus atom is bonded to three other phosphorus atoms, forming equilateral triangular faces with \(\mathrm{P-P-P}\) bond angles of \(60^\circ\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Each phosphorus atom in \(\mathrm{P_4}\) has three bond pairs and one lone pair of electrons, corresponding to an expected bond angle near \(90^\circ\)–\(109.5^\circ\) for unstrained \(p\) or \(sp^3\) orbitals.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Deviation of an actual bond angle from the ideal orbital angle creates angular strain in the molecule, which destabilises the bonds and lowers the activation energy required for chemical reactions.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Because the \(\mathrm{P-P-P}\) bond angle in the discrete \(\mathrm{P_4}\) tetrahedron is constrained to \(60^\circ\), there is severe angular strain. In contrast, red phosphorus is polymeric, consisting of chains of \(\mathrm{P_4}\) tetrahedra linked together, which relieves some strain and makes it far less reactive.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The \(60^\circ\) bond angle shown in the discrete \(\mathrm{P_4}\) tetrahedron causes high angular strain, making white phosphorus less stable and much more reactive than red phosphorus.

answer.text: It has a polymeric chain structure with strong \(\mathrm{P=P}\) double bonds.
It contains unpaired electrons that make it paramagnetic.
The \(\mathrm{P-P-P}\) bond angle is \(109.5^\circ\), causing high steric hindrance.
The \(\mathrm{P-P-P}\) bond angle is \(60^\circ\), resulting in high angular strain.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q03 - Haber process flow chart for ammonia manufacture

questiontext.text: Refer to the flow chart for the industrial manufacture of ammonia by Haber's process shown below. Identify the correct catalyst/promoter mixture (X) and operating pressure/temperature conditions used in the reactor.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The schematic represents Haber's process for synthesising ammonia from \(\mathrm{N_2(g)}\) and \(\mathrm{H_2(g)}\) via compression, catalytic conversion, condensation of liquid \(\mathrm{NH_3}\), and recycling of unreacted gases.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The reaction \(\mathrm{N_2(g) + 3H_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2NH_3(g)}\) has \(\Delta_f H^\circ = -46.1\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}\) (exothermic) and proceeds with a decrease in the number of gaseous moles (from 4 moles to 2 moles).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
According to Le Chatelier's principle, high pressure favours the forward reaction (fewer gaseous moles), and a moderate temperature is required so that both yield and reaction rate are practical.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
The optimum industrial conditions are a pressure of \(20\ \mathrm{MPa}\) (about \(200\ \mathrm{atm}\)), a temperature of \(\sim 700\ \mathrm{K}\), and a catalyst of iron oxide mixed with small amounts of \(\mathrm{K_2O}\) and \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\) to increase the rate of attainment of equilibrium.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Thus, the catalyst bed contains iron oxide with \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3} + \mathrm{K_2O}\) operating at \(20\ \mathrm{MPa}\) and \(700\ \mathrm{K}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q04 - Planar structure and bond parameters of gaseous nitric acid

questiontext.text: The planar molecular structure of nitric acid (\(\mathrm{HNO_3}\)) in the gaseous state is shown below with bond lengths and bond angles labelled. Which of the following correctly identifies the missing bond angle \(\theta\) and the shortest bond in this molecule?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The diagram shows gaseous \(\mathrm{HNO_3}\) as a planar molecule with \(\mathrm{H-O} = 96\ \mathrm{pm}\), \(\mathrm{O-N} = 140.6\ \mathrm{pm}\), terminal \(\mathrm{N-O} = 121\ \mathrm{pm}\), \(\angle \mathrm{H-O-N} = 102^\circ\), and the terminal \(\angle \mathrm{O-N-O}\) marked as \(\theta\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The two terminal \(\mathrm{N-O}\) bonds in \(\mathrm{HNO_3}\) are equivalent due to resonance, giving them partial double-bond character, whereas the \(\mathrm{N-OH}\) bond is a single bond.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Double-bond character increases electron density between the two terminal \(\mathrm{N-O}\) bonds, causing greater bond pair–bond pair repulsion between them and widening the \(\mathrm{O-N-O}\) angle beyond \(120^\circ\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Comparing the three distinct bond lengths shown in the diagram: \(\mathrm{H-O} = 96\ \mathrm{pm}\), terminal \(\mathrm{N-O} = 121\ \mathrm{pm}\), and \(\mathrm{N-OH} = 140.6\ \mathrm{pm}\). Clearly, the \(\mathrm{H-O}\) bond (\(96\ \mathrm{pm}\)) is the shortest bond. Due to repulsion between the two resonating \(\mathrm{N-O}\) bonds, the \(\mathrm{O-N-O}\) angle \(\theta\) opens up to \(130^\circ\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The bond angle \(\theta\) is \(130^\circ\), and the shortest bond in \(\mathrm{HNO_3}\) is the \(\mathrm{H-O}\) bond (\(96\ \mathrm{pm}\)).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q05 - Axial versus equatorial bond lengths in phosphorus pentachloride

questiontext.text: The trigonal bipyramidal structure of \(\mathrm{PCl_5}\) in the gaseous phase is shown below. Why are the two axial \(\mathrm{P-Cl}\) bonds (\(240\ \mathrm{pm}\)) longer than the three equatorial \(\mathrm{P-Cl}\) bonds (\(202\ \mathrm{pm}\))?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The diagram shows \(\mathrm{PCl_5}\) in a trigonal bipyramidal geometry with three equivalent equatorial \(\mathrm{P-Cl}\) bonds of length \(202\ \mathrm{pm}\) and two axial \(\mathrm{P-Cl}\) bonds of length \(240\ \mathrm{pm}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
In a trigonal bipyramidal arrangement, the three equatorial bonds lie in one plane at \(120^\circ\) to each other, while the two axial bonds lie perpendicular to this plane at \(90^\circ\) to each equatorial bond.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
According to VSEPR theory, electron-pair repulsions are much stronger at \(90^\circ\) than at \(120^\circ\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Each axial bond pair experiences three strong \(90^\circ\) repulsions from the three equatorial bond pairs. In contrast, each equatorial bond pair experiences only two \(90^\circ\) repulsions (from the two axial bond pairs) and two weaker \(120^\circ\) repulsions (from the other two equatorial bond pairs). Because the axial bond pairs suffer greater net repulsion, they are pushed further away from the central phosphorus atom, resulting in longer and weaker axial \(\mathrm{P-Cl}\) bonds (\(240\ \mathrm{pm}\) vs \(202\ \mathrm{pm}\)).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Axial \(\mathrm{P-Cl}\) bonds are longer than equatorial \(\mathrm{P-Cl}\) bonds because axial bond pairs suffer more repulsion than equatorial bond pairs.

answer.text: Equatorial bond pairs suffer more repulsion than axial bond pairs.
Axial bond pairs suffer more repulsion than equatorial bond pairs.
Phosphorus uses \(sp^3\) hybridisation for axial bonds and \(d\)-orbitals for equatorial bonds.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q06 - Basicity and structure of orthophosphorous acid

questiontext.text: Identify the oxoacid of phosphorus whose tetrahedral structure is shown below, and determine its basicity.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The diagram depicts a central phosphorus atom (\(\mathrm{P}\)) tetrahedrally bonded to one oxygen atom via a double bond (\(\mathrm{P=O}\)), one hydrogen atom directly (\(\mathrm{P-H}\)), and two hydroxyl groups (\(\mathrm{P-OH}\)).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Only hydrogen atoms attached to oxygen in \(\mathrm{P-OH}\) groups are ionisable in water to yield \(\mathrm{H^+}\) ions, whereas hydrogen atoms bonded directly to phosphorus (\(\mathrm{P-H}\)) are non-ionisable.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Counting the atoms gives the molecular formula \(\mathrm{H_3PO_3}\). The oxidation state of phosphorus is \(3(+1) + x + 3(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +3\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\(\mathrm{H_3PO_3}\) is orthophosphorous acid (phosphonic acid). Because it contains two \(\mathrm{P-OH}\) bonds and one \(\mathrm{P-H}\) bond, only two hydrogen atoms are ionisable. Therefore, its basicity is 2 (dibasic).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The structure corresponds to orthophosphorous acid (\(\mathrm{H_3PO_3}\)), which is dibasic (basicity = 2).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q07 - Structure and oxidation state of sulphur in peroxodisulphuric acid

questiontext.text: Examine the structure of peroxodisulphuric acid (\(\mathrm{H_2S_2O_8}\)) shown below. What is the oxidation state of each sulphur atom and how many \(\mathrm{S=O}\) bonds are present in one molecule?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The diagram shows peroxodisulphuric acid (\(\mathrm{H_2S_2O_8}\)), where two sulphur atoms are linked through a central peroxide bridge (\(-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{O}-\)). Each sulphur atom is bonded to two terminal \(=\mathrm{O}\) atoms, one \(-\mathrm{OH}\) group, and one oxygen of the peroxide bridge.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
In a peroxide linkage (\(-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{O}-\)), each oxygen atom has an oxidation state of \(-1\), whereas all other oxygen atoms (in \(\mathrm{S=O}\) and \(\mathrm{S-OH}\)) have an oxidation state of \(-2\), and hydrogen has \(+1\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The sum of oxidation numbers in a neutral molecule is zero: \[2(+1) + 2(x) + 6(-2) + 2(-1) = 0\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Solving for \(x\): \[2 + 2x - 12 - 2 = 0 \implies 2x = 12 \implies x = +6\] Counting the double bonds in the structure, each sulphur atom forms two \(\mathrm{S=O}\) double bonds, giving \(2 + 2 = 4\) \(\mathrm{S=O}\) bonds in total.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The oxidation state of each sulphur atom is \(+6\) (consistent with its maximum group oxidation state), and there are \(4\) \(\mathrm{S=O}\) bonds in one molecule.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q08 - Contact process flow diagram for sulphuric acid manufacture

questiontext.text: In the Contact Process flow diagram for the manufacture of sulphuric acid shown below, what is the purpose of unit P (arsenic purifier containing gelatinous hydrated ferric oxide) and what is the product Q collected from the absorption tower?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The flow diagram depicts the Contact Process: burning sulphur to produce \(\mathrm{SO_2}\), washing and drying the gas, passing it through the arsenic purifier (unit P), catalytically oxidising \(\mathrm{SO_2}\) to \(\mathrm{SO_3}\) over \(\mathrm{V_2O_5}\), and absorbing \(\mathrm{SO_3}\) in concentrated \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) to obtain product Q.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Catalysts such as \(\mathrm{V_2O_5}\) are sensitive to surface poisoning by impurities present in the reactant gas stream.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The key absorption reaction in the final tower is: \[\mathrm{SO_3(g)} + \mathrm{H_2SO_4(l)} \rightarrow \mathrm{H_2S_2O_7(l)}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
The \(\mathrm{SO_2}\) produced from burning sulphur or sulphide ores contains arsenic impurities that would poison the \(\mathrm{V_2O_5}\) catalyst in the catalytic converter; unit P removes these arsenic compounds. Then, \(\mathrm{SO_3}\) gas from the catalytic converter is absorbed in concentrated \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) to produce oleum (\(\mathrm{H_2S_2O_7}\)), which is later diluted with water to obtain \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) of desired concentration.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Unit P removes arsenic impurities to prevent poisoning of the \(\mathrm{V_2O_5}\) catalyst, and product Q is oleum (\(\mathrm{H_2S_2O_7}\)).

answer.text: Unit P: removes arsenic impurities to protect the \(\mathrm{V_2O_5}\) catalyst; Product Q: Oleum (\(\mathrm{H_2S_2O_7}\))

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q09 - Ring conformations and bond parameters of S8 and S6

questiontext.text: The molecular structures of two allotropic ring forms of sulphur, (I) \(\mathrm{S_8}\) and (II) cyclo-\(\mathrm{S_6}\), are shown below. Which of the following statements correctly describes their ring conformations and \(\mathrm{S-S-S}\) bond angles?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The diagrams show two cyclic allotropes of sulphur: (I) an 8-membered ring \(\mathrm{S_8}\) with \(\mathrm{S-S}\) bond length \(204\ \mathrm{pm}\) and \(\mathrm{S-S-S}\) bond angle \(107^\circ\), and (II) a 6-membered ring cyclo-\(\mathrm{S_6}\) with \(\mathrm{S-S}\) bond length \(205.7\ \mathrm{pm}\) and \(\mathrm{S-S-S}\) bond angle \(102.2^\circ\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Both \(\mathrm{S_8}\) (found in rhombic and monoclinic sulphur) and cyclo-\(\mathrm{S_6}\) adopt puckered non-planar ring conformations to minimise lone-pair and torsional strain.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
An 8-membered puckered ring \(\mathrm{S_8}\) adopts a crown shape, whereas a 6-membered puckered ring cyclo-\(\mathrm{S_6}\) adopts a chair form.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
From the molecular dimensions, \(\mathrm{S_8}\) has a crown-shaped puckered ring with a bond angle of \(107^\circ\), while cyclo-\(\mathrm{S_6}\) adopts a chair conformation with a slightly smaller bond angle of \(102.2^\circ\) and slightly longer \(\mathrm{S-S}\) bond (\(205.7\ \mathrm{pm}\)).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Therefore, \(\mathrm{S_8}\) has a crown shape with a \(107^\circ\) bond angle, and cyclo-\(\mathrm{S_6}\) has a chair form with a \(102.2^\circ\) bond angle.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q10 - Molecular shape and lone-pair placement in BrF3

questiontext.text: The VSEPR structure of bromine trifluoride (\(\mathrm{BrF_3}\)) is shown below. Which of the following correctly describes its hybridisation, molecular shape, and the positions occupied by the two lone pairs?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The diagram shows a central bromine atom (\(\mathrm{Br}\)) surrounded by three fluorine atoms (\(\mathrm{F}\)) and two lone pairs of electrons, with the two axial \(\mathrm{Br-F}\) bonds slightly bent toward the equatorial \(\mathrm{Br-F}\) bond.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
In a trigonal bipyramidal electron-pair arrangement, lone pairs occupy positions that minimise lone pair–lone pair and lone pair–bond pair repulsions (which follow the order \(\mathrm{lp-lp} > \mathrm{lp-bp} > \mathrm{bp-bp}\)).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Bromine has 7 valence electrons. Three form single bonds with three \(\mathrm{F}\) atoms, leaving 4 electrons as 2 lone pairs. Thus, steric number \(= 3 + 2 = 5\), corresponding to \(sp^3d\) hybridisation.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
The 5 electron pairs occupy the corners of a trigonal bipyramid. Placing both lone pairs in equatorial positions minimises \(\mathrm{lp-lp}\) and \(\mathrm{lp-bp}\) repulsions (only two \(90^\circ\) \(\mathrm{lp-bp}\) interactions per lone pair instead of three in an axial position). Furthermore, the two axial fluorine atoms bend slightly toward the equatorial fluorine to minimise repulsion from the two equatorial lone pairs, resulting in a slightly bent T-shaped molecular geometry.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Therefore, \(\mathrm{BrF_3}\) has \(sp^3d\) hybridisation, a bent T-shaped molecular geometry, and both lone pairs in equatorial positions.

answer.text: \(sp^3\), trigonal pyramidal, lone pairs in axial positions
\(sp^3d\), trigonal planar, lone pairs in axial positions
\(sp^3d^2\), square planar, one axial and one equatorial lone pair
\(sp^3d\), bent T-shaped, both lone pairs in equatorial positions

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q11 - Molecular geometry and hybridisation of xenon oxytetrafluoride

questiontext.text: The VSEPR structure of xenon oxytetrafluoride (\(\mathrm{XeOF_4}\)) is shown below. Identify the molecular geometry, the hybridisation of the central \(\mathrm{Xe}\) atom, and the number of lone pairs on \(\mathrm{Xe}\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The diagram shows a central xenon atom (\(\mathrm{Xe}\)) bonded to four coplanar fluorine atoms (\(\mathrm{F}\)) forming a square base, one oxygen atom (\(\mathrm{O}\)) via a double bond (\(\mathrm{Xe=O}\)) at the apex, and one lone pair of electrons opposite to the oxygen atom.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
In VSEPR theory, a double bond counts as one \(\sigma\)-bonding region (electron domain) when determining steric number and hybridisation.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Xenon has 8 valence electrons. Four electrons form 4 \(\mathrm{Xe-F}\) single bonds, and two electrons form the \(\mathrm{Xe=O}\) double bond, leaving 2 electrons as 1 lone pair. Thus, the number of \(\sigma\)-bond pairs is \(4 + 1 = 5\) and the number of lone pairs is \(1\), giving a steric number of \(5 + 1 = 6\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
A steric number of 6 corresponds to \(sp^3d^2\) hybridisation and an octahedral electron-pair arrangement. With 5 bonding domains (4 \(\mathrm{F}\) atoms in a square plane and 1 \(\mathrm{O}\) atom at an axial position) and 1 lone pair occupying the opposite axial position, the resulting molecular geometry is square pyramidal.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Therefore, \(\mathrm{XeOF_4}\) has a square pyramidal molecular geometry, \(sp^3d^2\) hybridisation, and 1 lone pair on the central \(\mathrm{Xe}\) atom.
